task_row_model.query: What year did the Berlin Wall fall, and which two German states were reunified after its fall?

documents.content: Academic analysis of late-20th-century German history often highlights the pivotal date of 9 November 1989, when the Berlin Wall effectively ceased to divide the city. Mass protests in East Berlin and a mistaken announcement by an East German official led to crossings being opened that evening. Historians situate this event within a broader sequence of 1989 popular movements across Eastern Europe, and occasionally reference earlier Cold War episodes such as the 1948–49 Berlin Blockade as background context.

Reference entry: The formal political reunification of Germany occurred under West Germany's Basic Law when the German Democratic Republic (GDR, often called East Germany) acceded to the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG, West Germany) on 3 October 1990. This legal process used Article 23 procedures to incorporate the five new federal states from the East into the Federal Republic, resulting in a single German state. Entries on constitutional law provide definitional boilerplate about accession procedures; unrelated examples in the same compendium discuss Austrian neutrality as a comparative case.

News-style memoir: Berliners celebrated at the Brandenburg Gate when walls came down, lighting bonfires and dancing amid a sudden rush of visitors. Tourism numbers rose sharply through 1990 as the city reopened to Western and Eastern travelers, and informal gatherings marked both relief and uncertainty about the political future. Journalists at the time wrote speculative commentary on what reunification might mean for housing and local businesses, while human-interest pieces focused on family reunions and the symbolic toppling of checkpoints.

Informal historical note: The term 'Iron Curtain' is commonly used to describe postwar East–West divisions, and scholars sometimes include economic and military statistics when discussing the era—e.g., defense spending comparisons and emigration figures. Such adjacent terminology and loosely related statistics often appear alongside broader narratives of Soviet collapse; unrelated case studies in these notes occasionally compare the German situation to the Korean Demilitarized Zone to illustrate divided nations.

task_row_model.golden_answer: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989. Following that, the German Democratic Republic (GDR, East Germany) and the Federal Republic of Germany (FRG, West Germany) were formally reunified on 3 October 1990, merging the two German states into a single Federal Republic of Germany.
